summary: The proposal contains a critical violation of the page limit and several major structural and writing issues, notably overly brief objective subsections and a paragraph that mixes multiple ideas. Minor passive‑voice usage is also noted. Significant revisions are required before the proposal can be submitted.

findings.title: Proposal exceeds allowed page limit
findings.description: The proposal spans 12 pages, exceeding the maximum of 6 pages specified.

findings.title: Objective subsections are too short
findings.description: Each objective subsection (4.1–4.4) contains only a single paragraph; the guidelines require at least two paragraphs per subsection.

locations.quote: 4.2 **Enforce** an Expiry Date on Every Grant
4.3 **Delegate** the Approval of Requests to Maintainers

**I model the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves bound to target systems, as the UML object diagram in Figure 2 shows. One approval on a folder covers every resource beneath it, including later additions. A transitive‑closure table stores the tree, and a fan‑out cap keeps an approval on the root from provisioning the whole infrastructure.**

findings.title: Paragraph mixes multiple ideas
findings.description: A paragraph in the Problem section combines distinct topics (persistent access, audit consequences, and historical traceability) instead of focusing on a single coherent idea, violating the one‑idea‑per‑paragraph rule.

locations.quote: **Access never ends. Nobody records when a person stops needing access, so access piles up, and former students keep login access to the compute hosts long after they leave, a decay that studies of enterprises report as well [Ker+02, SMJ01].** Auditors bear the consequence: the history lies scattered across systems and chat logs, and nobody can say who had access to a host last March and who approved it.

findings.title: Passive voice usage
findings.description: The sentence uses passive voice ('written after I freeze the framework'), which conflicts with the active voice requirement.

locations.quote: I reach this objective when the webhook connector, **written after I freeze the framework**, needs one new class and one registry entry.
